title: Accrued Earnings and Growth: Implications for Future Profitability and Market Mispricing

models.sample_description: Firm-year observations from 1964–1993 with the prior, current, and subsequent financial-statement data required for ROA and net-operating-asset growth. Table 3 reports 32,961 firm-years aggregated across 30 annual regressions; annual regression sample sizes vary.
models.method_reported: Annual regressions in the style of Fama and MacBeth (1973)
models.method_details: The paper states that it estimates annual regressions and reports t-statistics from the means and standard deviations of 30 annual parameter estimates; it does not name the estimator used within each annual regression.
models.equation_text: Equation (2): ROA_(t+1) = beta_0 + beta_1*GrLTNOA_t + beta_2*ACC_t + beta_3*ROA_t + e_(t+1).

standard_errors.details: The coefficient t-statistics are based on the means and standard deviations of the parameter estimates from 30 annual regressions.

evidence.quote: As in Fama and MacBeth (1973), we estimate annual regressions and report t-statistics based on the means and standard deviations of the parameter estimates obtained in 30 annual regressions.
The t-statistics are based on the averages and standard deviations of the 30 parameter estimates obtained in the annual regressions.

estimation_procedure.description: Estimate a separate cross-sectional regression in each of 30 years from 1964 through 1993; report average coefficients and t-statistics based on the annual parameter estimates.

evidence.quote: As in Fama and MacBeth (1973), we estimate annual regressions and report t-statistics based on the means and standard deviations of the parameter estimates obtained in 30 annual regressions.
The coefficients and adjusted R2 are averages obtained from the 30 annual regressions from 1964 to 1993 (32,961 firm-years).

review_notes: Retained as the principal direct future-profitability family. The later joint market-pricing system is not a construction dependency of this regression.

missing_fields.method: The source describes annual regressions and Fama–MacBeth-style inference but does not identify the estimator used within each annual regression.

dependent_variable.name: ROA_{t+1}
dependent_variable.definition: One-year-ahead return on assets: operating income after depreciation and amortization at t+1 divided by average total assets at t+1.

evidence.quote: ROA_(t+1) is operating income after depreciation and amortization at t+1 divided by average total assets at t+1; ROA_t similarly uses time-t income and average assets.

independent_variables.name: GrLTNOA_t
independent_variables.definition: One-year growth in long-term net operating assets, defined as GrNOA_t minus ACC_t and deflated by contemporaneous average total assets. GrNOA is annual change in NOA, where NOA = AR + INV + OTHERCA + PPE + INTANG + OTHERLTA - AP - OTHERCL - OTHERLTL. GrLTNOA therefore reduces to changes in operating asset/liability elements excluded from ACC, including changes in net PPE and intangibles exclusive of depreciation and amortization, other long-term assets, and other long-term liabilities.
independent_variables.formula: GrLTNOA_t = [(NOA_t - NOA_(t-1)) / AVG(TA_(t-1), TA_t)] - ACC_t; NOA_t = AR_t + INV_t + OTHERCA_t + PPE_t + INTANG_t + OTHERLTA_t - AP_t - OTHERCL_t - OTHERLTL_t

evidence.quote: GrNOA_t = NOA_t - NOA_(t-1). NOA_t = AR_t + INV_t + OTHERCA_t + PPE_t + INTANG_t + OTHERLTA_t - AP_t - OTHERCL_t - OTHERLTL_t.

GrLTNOA_t = GrNOA_t - ACC_t. GrNOA and GrLTNOA are deflated by contemporaneous average total assets. PPE is net property plant and equipment item 8; INTANG is intangibles item 33; OTHERLTA is other long-term assets item 69; OTHERLTL is other long-term liabilities item 75. The source explains that GrLTNOA reduces to changes in the operating asset and liability elements excluded from ACC, including DeltaPPE and DeltaINTANG exclusive of depreciation and amortization, DeltaOTHERLTA and DeltaOTHERLTL.

independent_variables.name: ACC_t
independent_variables.definition: Operating accruals: change in operating working capital (changes in accounts receivable, inventories, and other current assets less changes in accounts payable and other current liabilities), minus current-period depreciation and amortization expense; ACC is deflated by contemporaneous average total assets. Compustat items are AR 2, INV 3, OTHERCA 68, AP 70, OTHERCL 72, DEPAMORT 14. Tax payable and deferred taxes are excluded. The authors note possible interest accruals in OTHERCL and report robustness to excluding it.
independent_variables.formula: ACC_t = [(DeltaAR_t + DeltaINV_t + DeltaOTHERCA_t) - (DeltaAP_t + DeltaOTHERCL_t) - DEPAMORT_t] / AVG(TA_(t-1), TA_t)

evidence.quote: ACC_t = GrWC_t - DEPAMORT_t. GrWC_t = (DeltaAR_t + DeltaINV_t + DeltaOTHERCA_t) - (DeltaAP_t + DeltaOTHERCL_t). Components are changes in Compustat AR item 2, inventories 3, other current assets 68, accounts payable 70, other current liabilities 72; DEPAMORT is depreciation and amortization expense item 14.
ACC and CFO are deflated by contemporaneous average total assets.

Taxes payable and deferred taxes are excluded because operating income excludes tax expense; the footnote discusses the remaining possible inclusion of interest accruals within other current liabilities.

independent_variables.definition: Current-period return on assets: operating income after depreciation and amortization (OPINC, Compustat item 178) divided by contemporaneous average total assets (TA, Compustat item 6).

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
Sample Selection

Our sample consists of firms with required financial statement and returns data for the
30-year period from 1964 to 1993. This sample period ensures replication of Sloan’s (1996)
results using a similar research design and 30-year sample period. <sup>3</sup> We extract the financial

data from the annual database of Standard & Poor’s 2000 Compustat Industrial and Merged
Industrial Research files. We obtain the stock price and share data from the Center for
Research in Security Prices (CRSP) 2001 monthly stock price database.

We cannot directly estimate the accrual and cash flow components of operating income
for years prior to the enactment of SFAS No. 95 in 1988. Thus, we follow Sloan (1996)
and use an indirect (balance sheet) approach that relies on the articulation between changes
in working capital and accruals. <sup>4</sup>

We eliminate the sample firm-years without sufficient financial data to compute operating income, accruals, cash flows, or net operating assets. There are 38,865 firm-years
with stock price data and sufficient data to estimate the financial statement variables. Since
we use the indirect method to estimate accruals, we also eliminate firm-years that would
most likely induce noise into the measurement of accruals: (1) Compustat footnote codes
suggest that working capital components are estimated since the company reports an unclassified balance sheet (2,563 firm-years); (2) Compustat footnote codes suggest that managers of the firm made voluntary accounting changes that affect either operating income or
working capital accounts (2,635 firm-years); and (3) goodwill (Compustat item 240) increased from year to year since, in purchase business combinations, changes in the balance
sheet accounts may not articulate with income statement accruals (706 firm-years). The
sample selection process results in a final sample of 32,961 firm-years with available stock
price and financial statement data in prior, current, and subsequent years.
